Forty years I've held Nell's secret. Forty years of watching Bram Holloway pace that boundary line, of hearing Wren fret over markers moved by wind or time, of saying nothing.

The saw calls louder than conscience. First light's come and gone already, and I've timber standing that's waited longer than any grudge.

The day's burning, I've no food, and standing here with Nell and Corwin both is costing us all. I need to move—sell this timber, get to where there's bread, keep my word while keeping my household fed.

"Corwin," I say to him before I go, "you heard me. Answer or don't. But I'm owed for my wood, and I've none to eat." I turn from them both and walk toward the timber yard. The weight of Nell's presence follows, but I've said what I'll say. Forty years holds or it breaks on its own.
